newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-CIPOLLINI HAS SHORTS FOR EVERY OCCASION.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-CIPOLLINI HAS SHORTS FOR EVERY OCCASION.

text.p: Mario Cipollini, fashion model of the Tour de France, seems as concerned about his flashy shorts as his fast finishes as he bids to hold his early lead.
The Italian started the first stage of the Tour on Sunday wearing shorts the colour of the American flag to please his sponsor. At the finish he was able to sport a yellow jersey on his back.
Ex-model Cipollini first signalled how much he cared for his appearance two years ago when he insisted on wearing shorts the colour of the Italian flag after winning his national champinship.
He was repeatedly fined by the International Cycling Union (UCI) which insists on riders wearing their team's shorts but he refused to comply.
After producing a superb surge to win the opening stage from Forges-les-Eaux to Rouen, Cipollini said he had shorts for every occasion during the Tour.

"We've thought about every possibility. I brought yellow shorts just in case but also green ones for the points leader jersey and also black ones," said the Saeco team leader, winner of five stages in the recent Giro d'Italia.
Even though he likes the colour and hopes to stick to it for as long as he can, Cipollini is aware he will not bring the yellow jersey back to Paris. But he has other plans.
"To reach Paris with the green jersey on would be a great achievement. But I must first discuss with my employers as they want me to ride in the Vuelta as well," he said.
"Three big Tours in a row would be too much," he added.
Cipollini, who broke some hearts when he married a few years ago and is now a father, wore the yellow jersey for a couple of days in 1993.
But he said it was not his favourite outfit. "The Giro pink jersey is my favourite because Italy is where my heart is," he said.
But elegance has nothing to do with his sprinting abilities. Aged 30, Cipollini has never been stronger and he thinks experience has a lot to do with it.
"I had more stamina a few years ago. But now I'm good all round and at 30, against younger riders, I must say I don't often make mistakes," he said.
Now the Italian, who has won five Tour de France stages in five outings, hopes to do even better.
"I have never won a stage with the yellow jersey on. That's what I hope to do now. Maybe tomorrrow?"
